summary_rationale: Bloom has a differentiated, commercially deployed solid-oxide onsite-power platform, named repeat customers, a growing service base, and rapid 2026 product revenue and operating-income expansion. However, business quality remains strictly conditional after forensic audit of 2026 SEC filings: (1) two customers generated 66% of 9M 2026 revenue (69% in Q3 2026) and U.S. sales reached 97% in Q3, with the 23% related-party share tied to Brookfield AI Fund JVs amid explicit 10-Q warnings on neocloud/AI tenant credit risk and air-permit pauses; (2) long-term take-or-pay supplier commitments of $5.8 billion ($2.6 billion due in FY2027) and $327.0 million in vendor advances far exceed $661.2 million in long-term product/installation RPO; (3) 9M 2026 gross margin benefited from a non-recurring $37.2 million IEEPA tariff refund (replaced in July 2026 by 10%–12.5% tariffs) while accrued warranty liabilities jumped 251% to $70.3 million on a $42.5 million specific reserve and installation margin remained negative (-4.8% in Q3 2026); (4) $306.5 million of Oracle warrant consideration assets will drag future recognized revenue; (5) diluted shares rose 38.0% YoY to 324.3 million while executive PSUs reward revenue and non-GAAP product margin without FCF, ROIC, or installation-margin accountability alongside three CFO transitions in 12 months; and (6) supply-chain scrutiny (Hunterbrook scandium-oxide class action and Plansee/GTP arbitration) remains active. Sustained post-capex, post-working-capital free cash flow through a full deployment cycle is not yet established.
